decision.summary: The Federal Reserve raised the benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to a target range of 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent.

changes.quote: Recent data suggest that growth rates of household spending and business fixed investment have moderated from their strong fourth-quarter readings.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted that consumer spending and business investments slowed down somewhat after very strong results late last year.

changes.quote: The economic outlook has strengthened in recent months.
changes.explanation: The Committee feels more confident overall about the direction of the economy.

changes.quote: In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent.
changes.explanation: Because the job market and inflation are behaving as anticipated, officials chose to increase borrowing costs.

tone_quotes.quote: The economic outlook has strengthened in recent months.
The Committee expects that economic conditions will evolve in a manner that will warrant further gradual increases in the federal funds rate

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 13.16% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.89% and moved 0 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.46% would not change.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 4.1%, and employers added an average of 227k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.3% over the past year (February 2018); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 4.6% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -3 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.18%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.46% on the day.

card.whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed intends to keep raising interest rates gradually as long as the economy performs well. Educational forecast models suggest a 71% probability of holding rates steady at the next meeting.
